newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CLOSING DEBT MARKET REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CLOSING DEBT MARKET REPORT.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed lower for the first time in nine trading sessions after benign U.S. inflation data failed to impress offshore markets.
Guilder paper eased by more than its German equivalents, slighting narrowing the yield differential to Germany which had widened over the previous two weeks.
The 5.75 percent February 2007 state loan, the new 10-year Dutch benchmark, was actively traded, ending at a bid yield of 5.39 percent, up from 5.36 percent the previous day.
"We did have some selling at the longer end today, more profit taking than anything else," said one dealer.
The closing yield on the new issue has fallen from 5.74 percent since January 29.
The Dutch bond market opened lower, regained most of its losses by the midsession, but succumbed to a sell-off in the afternoon.
Dealers said the impetus was the reaction of U.S. Treasuries and German Bunds, which initially edged up on lower than forecast U.S. January inflation data, before dipping.
Consumer prices rose 0.1 percent, less than the forecast of 0.3 percent. Taken with last week's producer price index, analysts said it indicated U.S. inflation remained benign.
One dealer said the reaction was a good indication of the state of world bond markets.
"It means there's a lot of bullish news already discounted (into prices)," he said, adding he would not be surprised to see a continued sell-off.
A broker who reporting selling interest mainly among longer paper said the Dutch market appeared nervous.
"To start with, people felt bullish but that's been shaken out in the afternoon," he said.
A trader said the market may have peaked for the short term but continued positive U.S. data should prevent more losses.
